Article Title: Anthropic launches personal finance feature in Claude, lets users connect bank accounts for money insights
Article Text:
Claude Personal Finance feature: What it does

Focus on privacy and security

No ads or product sales

Getting started and what’s next

After ChatGPT-maker OpenAI, now AI giant Anthropic has introduced personal finance feature to its chatbot Claude. Anthropic has announced the roll out of Personal Finance feature for its AI assistant Claude, enabling users to connect bank and card accounts and also ask questions about their finances in natural language. The company also said that the feature is created to help users get to better understand their spending, balances and transactions without switching between multiple banking apps. Presently, the company is rolling out the feature only for beta subscribers on Claude's Pro, Max and Ultra plans in the United States. As per Anthropic, users can now securely connect their financial accounts and also receive answers about their money, with Claude offering explanations in everyday language.Users can ask questions such as where their money went this month, whether they are spending more than they earn, or what an APR is and how much interest they have been charged this year. Claude answers from the connected accounts’ balances and transactions, in everyday language, and explains unfamiliar terms. In an example from Anthropic, a user ten days from payday asks where their money went. Claude totals spending across linked accounts and sorts it by category.It then checks previous months, flags a membership renewal, and lists four payments due from checking before payday along with the amount that will be left.Claude can also look across all linked accounts for things that are easy to miss, such as duplicate charges, unexpected fees or a bill that has crept up over the year. Users can ask for a weekly spending chart, a calendar of what’s due or a dashboard of chosen numbers, and keep adjusting it.Anthropic emphasised that the new feature provides read-only access to financial data and cannot move, manage or invest a user's money. The company also noted that Personal Finance is not designed to provide investment advice and that users should verify important figures directly with their banks. Account connectivity is powered by financial data network Plaid, which allows users to authenticate directly with their banks. Anthropic said Claude does not see or request users' banking passwords. For connected accounts, Claude can access information such as account names, balances, credit limits and up to two years of transaction history.The company added that conversations conducted within the Personal Finance hub are not used to train its AI models. Users can also disconnect their accounts at any time, after which Claude can no longer access the associated dataAnthropic said Personal Finance carries no ads or sponsored recommendations. It also does not offer credit cards, loans or savings accounts of its own, so users get a straight answer.Users who see Personal Finance in Claude’s sidebar can connect one account and ask a question, such as whether they can afford a trip this spring. Setup steps are in the Help Center.Anthropic called the launch a first step. For bigger financial decisions, it said, people are best served by Claude working alongside licensed professionals and regulated firms. The company said it is exploring how to enable that and wants to hear from banks, wealth managers and financial services firms that want to help shape it.
Article Summary: Users can connect bank and card accounts and also ask questions about their finances in natural language. Claude answers from the connected accounts’ balances and transactions, in everyday language, and explains unfamiliar terms. Users can ask for a weekly spending chart, a calendar of what’s due or a dashboard of chosen numbers, and keep adjusting it.

Article Title: Yale launches Solis Safe Series in India, prices start at Rs 19,999
Article Text:
Focus on security and smart access

Convenience features for everyday use

Multiple sizes, three-year warranty

Pricing and availability

Yale, part of ASSA ABLOY, has expanded its home security portfolio in India with the launch of the new Solis Safe Series, a premium range of digital safes aimed at modern households seeking advanced protection for valuables such as jewellery, important documents, cash and family heirlooms. The company said the new range has been developed to address the growing demand for technology-driven home security solutions as consumers increasingly invest in connected homes and premium interiors. The Solis Safe Series combines security features, smart access options and contemporary design to make personal security a seamless part of modern living.The Yale Solis Safe Series features a minimalist design with a premium touch panel intended to blend into contemporary home interiors. The safes are built using precision-engineered, laser-cut construction and include an ultra-tight-fitting door and body to help improve resistance against forced-entry attempts. A motorised locking mechanism provides an additional layer of protection for stored valuables. One of the key highlights of the new range is its multiple authentication options. Users can unlock the safes using fingerprint recognition or a personalised PIN code, while dual authentication is available for enhanced security.The safes can store up to 25 fingerprints and also include two mechanical override keys for emergency access.Yale has also integrated a number of convenience-focused features into the new series. These include interior LED lighting for improved visibility, a digital display and low-battery alerts to help users monitor power levels. The safes operate on four AA alkaline batteries and feature an external battery compartment along with emergency battery access, ensuring users can access the safe even if the primary batteries are depleted.Commenting on the launch, a Yale India spokesperson said the company aimed to combine advanced security, intuitive technology and premium design in a product that aligns with the evolving expectations of homeowners. “The way consumers approach home security is evolving. Today, homeowners are looking for solutions that not only offer reliable protection but also integrate effortlessly into their everyday lives. With the Solis Safe Series, our focus has been on bringing together advanced security, intuitive technology and premium design,” the spokesperson said.The Solis Safe Series is available in multiple sizes to suit varying storage requirements, ranging from small personal items to larger collections of valuables. Yale is offering a three-year warranty across the range. According to the company, the launch reflects its continued focus on providing security solutions tailored to increasingly design-conscious and technology-oriented Indian consumers.The Yale Solis Safe Series is available in four variants:* Solis 250 – Rs 19,999* Solis 230 Laptop – Rs 22,999* Solis 400 – Rs 24,999* Solis 560 – Rs 30,999All models are available through Yale India’s official online store. Prices are inclusive of taxes and may vary depending on promotional offers.
Article Summary: The Yale Solis Safe Series features a minimalist design with a premium touch panel intended to blend into contemporary home interiors. The safes are built using precision-engineered, laser-cut construction and include an ultra-tight- fitting door and body. Yale is offering a three-year warranty across the range.

Article Title: Experts in Canada are testing doorbell cameras' for Polar bears, called Bear-vision, they combine radar and cameras to …
Article Text:
Image Credit: Alan Wilson/Wikipedia

How will Bear-vision work

Why is Churchill’s waste facility the first location

Why are bears spending longer near communities

What other tools are researchers testing

“It’s not easy to live with large predators as your neighbours, so we’re investing in coexistence approaches, especially as we see climate change causing more human-bear encounters. By developing and field-testing innovative, non-lethal deterrents like drones and detection tech like Bear-vision, we’re hoping to expand the variety of safe, effective, and affordable coexistence tools available to communities,”

Researchers are testing Bear-vision cameras to warn communities in Canada about approaching polar bears. Conservation charity Polar Bears International is developing Bear-vision, a warning system built on security camera technology that can be paired with shorter-range radar. Its first deployment is planned at Churchill’s waste facility this autumn to help monitor bears and reduce surprise encounters, the organisation’ noted in a blog post.The camera is intended to offer a more affordable, easy-to-use alternative to wide-area radar systems. Researchers will use data gathered at the site to train it to recognise polar bears and send notifications when they appear. The project comes as bears gather along Hudson Bay, waiting for sea ice to return so they can hunt seals, while communities work to keep people and wildlife safely apart.Bear-vision builds on the organisation’s earlier Bear-dar detection work. While Bear-dar monitors wider areas using radar, the new system uses smart security camera technology and can incorporate shorter-range radar.​Polar Bears International compares the intended function to a doorbell camera that alerts residents when a polar bear is outside. The Churchill deployment will help researchers gather the information needed to train the notification system.Churchill began working with Polar Bears International to keep bears out of its dump after a fire destroyed its waste facilities. Garbage can attract bears looking for food, creating risks for both the animals and people nearby.The response includes new electric fences, Bear-dar and Bear-vision monitoring, and a visit by a Churchill delegation to a waste management facility in Greenland. The camera trial is part of a broader effort to manage the site, not replace physical barriers or other measures.Polar Bears International says climate-driven sea ice loss leaves bears waiting on land about a month longer than their grandparents did. The ice-free period around Hudson Bay now lasts three to four weeks longer than in the 1980s, placing additional strain on their stored fat reserves.The organisation says these longer periods ashore make coexistence measures increasingly important. Its Polar Bear Week, running November 1–7, coincides with the seasonal gathering near Churchill.Polar Bears International and Brigham Young University are also working with Churchill’s Polar Bear Alert Program to test drones as an affordable, non-lethal way to move bears away from communities. That separate deterrent project includes ultrasonic sound, conductive materials and a new odour-based bear spray formula.said Geoff York, Polar Bears International’s vice president of science and policy.
Article Summary: Polar Bears International is developing Bear-vision, a warning system built on security camera technology that can be paired with shorter-range radar. Its first deployment is planned at Churchill’s waste facility this autumn. Researchers will use data gathered at the site to train it to recognise polar bears and send notifications when they appear.

Article Title: Rhode Island turned four-lane roads into three-lane “road diets”; a safety analysis found 29% fewer crashes and 37% fewer fatal or injury crashes
Article Text:
AI Representation: A three-lane road configuration with a dedicated centre turn lane. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Rhode Island’s evaluation found a reduction in total and injury crashes

Safety Effectiveness of the Road Diet Treatment in Rhode Island In

A three-lane layout separates turning vehicles from through traffic

Virginia research found similar reductions, with bicycle lanes

Development of Road Diet Segment and Intersection Crash Modification Factors,

RIDOT installed a road diet on Main Avenue in Warwick

Route 113 in Warwick, Rhode Island. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Four-lane roads can create conflicts when vehicles slow down or cross traffic to turn. Rhode Island addressed these risks by converting selected roads into three-lane layouts. The changes left one through lane in each direction and added a centre lane for left turns. A state-specific evaluation found fewer crashes after the conversions, including crashes involving fatalities or injuries.Yuying Zhou, Scott Himes, Thanh Le, Jeff Gooch, Kayla Northup and Peter Pavao published Transportation Research Record in 2022 . The assessment involved the installation of road diets in Rhode Island and the calculation of crash modification factors (CMFs), which are measures of change in the number of crashes that occur due to a road treatment. The results were a CMF of 0.71 for all crashes, which equates to a 29% reduction. For fatal and injury crashes, or KABC crashes, which cover fatal, incapacitating, non-incapacitating and possible injury crashes but not property damage-only crashes, the CMF was 0.63, equating to a 37% reduction.The FHWA’s Rhode Island Highway Safety Improvement Program report describes the state’s CMF development process as based on the regression cross-section method.The Rhode Island evaluation was a regression-based before-and-after analysis of road diets installed before the study’s 2022 publication, so it could not have drawn on post-installation data from the Main Avenue project, which was completed in October 2022. There is no evidence of an untreated control group or an empirical Bayes process in the summary provided.Federal guidance also defines a traditional road diet as the conversion of an undivided four-lane road into a three-lane road. The centre lane provides room for motorists to slow down before making left turns without stopping in the through lane. This helps avoid potential issues with unexpected lane changes and slowing down due to turning traffic. The available space provided by eliminating the through lane can be used for cycling lanes, pedestrian islands, transit purposes, or parking.Linda Lim and Michael D. Fontaine examined road diet safety inpublished in Transportation Research Record in 2022 . The study encompassed 36 road segments and 39 intersections that had undergone road diets from 2009 to 2018. The road diets included bicycle lanes, so the results reflect the entire treatment rather than lane striping alone.In terms of road segments, the FHWA Crash Modification Factors Clearinghouse lists the Virginia study’s CMFs as 0.62 for total crashes and 0.36 for fatal and injury crashes, which correspond to reductions of 38% and 64%. For intersections, the same clearinghouse entry reports CMFs of 0.65 for total crashes and 0.54 for fatal and injury crashes, which correspond to reductions of 35% and 46%. There was no safety benefit found at unsignalized intersections. Similar to the Rhode Island Study mentioned above, the findings from the Virginia study demonstrate a reduction in the number of crashes after road diet treatments. However, since the two studies were conducted in different settings and designs, those percentages cannot be generalised.The Rhode Island Department of Transportation’s (RIDOT) October 11, 2022, travel advisory stated that the agency planned to install a road diet on Main Avenue (Route 113) between Route 5 and Jefferson Boulevard in Warwick during the week of October 17, with the three-lane section running between Bailey Street and Sycamore Avenue. Bad weather delayed the work and the new traffic configuration was expected to be in place by the morning of October 20. The new road design was implemented on October 20. The agency also conducted other road diets throughout the state.RIDOT indicated speeding, crashes and narrow roads as some of its concerns. According to the review, there were 59 crashes in the previous five years, out of which one was fatal and 14 caused injuries. The new design would lead to 25 seconds of additional travel time on average. The agency stated in 2022 that it would review the project and cooperate with the City of Warwick and that this review would be conducted separately from the statewide safety analysis. The 29% and 37% reductions come from the Rhode Island evaluation and not from any post-installation results for Main Avenue.The Rhode Island findings suggest that the road diets can help reduce crashes and improve safety on roads with suitable conditions. The research from Virginia found some reduction, but in their case, they had the bicycle lanes included in the treatment. Neither study has proven that all four-lane roads will have the same outcome.
Article Summary: Rhode Island’s evaluation found a reduction in total and injury crashes. A three-lane layout separates turning vehicles from through traffic. Virginia research found similar reductions, with bicycle lanes. There was no safety benefit found at unsignalized intersections.

Article Title: Cancer patient came up with a fundraising idea at his kitchen table during treatment; 21 years later, his UK platform has raised more than £50 million for charities
Article Text:

How did a cancer patient develop the fundraising idea during treatment

Easyfundraising turns online shopping into charitable fundraising

How can shoppers support charities without spending extra money

How does easyfundraising help charities and good causes of all sizes

An idea formed during cancer treatment and worked out at a kitchen table has become one of the UK’s biggest charity shopping platforms. Ian Woodroffe founded easyfundraising after seeing a chance to join charitable fundraising to the UK’s growing e-commerce industry. It launched officially in 2005. Supporters raise money for charities and good causes just by shopping online through participating brands, so they never make a separate donation. The company’s website says easyfundraising has now raised over £50 million for more than 180,000 charities and good causes across the UK.The idea originated during a conversation at a New Year's Eve party in 2002. However, it was during his cancer treatment that founder Ian Woodroffe developed the concept of connecting fundraising with the growing UK e-commerce sector.The company explains that Woodroffe had developed a new understanding of the importance of fundraising for charities and good causes during a critical period in his life. This experience inspired him to create an accessible way for people to support charitable organisations. His vision was to establish an easy and free fundraising method that would help causes receive much-needed financial support. The concept also reflected his belief that everyday online shopping could become an opportunity to make a positive difference.By allowing shoppers to raise donations without paying anything extra, Woodroffe aimed to remove financial barriers to charitable giving. This approach eventually helped turn an ordinary consumer activity into a practical fundraising opportunity for charities across the UK.The idea was developed around Woodroffe's kitchen table before easyfundraising officially launched in 2005. The platform was built around the concept of combining online shopping with charitable fundraising, allowing people to support causes through purchases they were already making.Easyfundraising was established to provide a free way for charities and good causes across the UK to raise funds. Rather than requiring supporters to make additional donations, its model connects online shoppers with brands that give back to their chosen causes through the platform.The platform has raised more than £50 million for over 180,000 charities and good causes since its launch. Its model works by connecting supporters who want to contribute to charitable organisations with participating brands that provide donations through online shopping.The company describes its mission as turning everyday spending into a force for good. People can choose a cause they want to support, browse participating brands and shop online through easyfundraising. The platform provides a way to generate funds for their chosen causes through these purchases without requiring shoppers to donate additional money themselves.Easyfundraising aims to make fundraising technology accessible to charities and good causes of all sizes. Its platform supports a range of organisations, from local football teams and children's schools to national charities. The company says its mission is to provide technology that makes fundraising easier and helps organisations continue their work.Its purpose is to make giving part of everyday life rather than a separate activity. With an expanding list of participating brands, easyfundraising continues to connect shoppers, businesses and charitable organisations through its online platform. Its stated mission is to help people turn ordinary spending into financial support for the causes they care about.
Article Summary: Easyfundraising was established to provide a free way for charities and good causes across the UK to raise funds. Rather than requiring supporters to make additional donations, its model connects online shoppers with brands that give back to their chosen causes through the platform. The platform has raised more than £50 million for over 180,000 charities since its launch in 2005.

Article Title: Luke Bryan began taking his concerts to working farms in 2009; by the end of his 2026 Farm Tour, the project had awarded 97 college scholarships, while a sponsor-linked campaign had provided over 11 m
Article Text:
Photo credit: Luke Bryan / Instagram

A tour built around farms

Scholarships for farming families

More than 11 million meals

Fans contributed food too

A broader commitment to community

The 2026 tour in context

Luke Bryan began taking his concerts to working farms in 2009 with a simple idea: bring live country music to the communities that help feed the country. By the close of his 17th Farm Tour in September 2026, the project had awarded 97 college scholarships and helped provide more than 11 million meals, according to Luke Bryan’s official website and a report by AG Daily on Yahoo Entertainment.The 2026 edition continued the tour’s long-running partnership with Bayer through the #HerestotheFarmer campaign. It combined concerts in rural settings with practical support for farming families, local food banks and students pursuing higher education near the tour stops. Read more about it here:The Farm Tour was created to put Bryan’s shows directly into agricultural communities rather than limiting them to arenas and amphitheatres. Since its launch in 2009, the tour has visited working farms across the United States, turning fields and farm properties into temporary concert venues. That setting matters because it keeps the music connected to the people and places it celebrates. Bryan’s audience is often made up of rural residents, agricultural workers and families whose livelihoods depend on farming, making the tour feel less like a travelling spectacle and more like a local gathering.The 2026 run marked the 17th Farm Tour and concluded in September. By that point, the initiative had grown from a novel concert format into a sustained programme with measurable benefits for students, food-insecure households and rural communities.One of the tour’s most lasting contributions has been its scholarship programme. Since 2009, Bryan has awarded 97 college scholarships to students from farming families who are attending local colleges or universities near Farm Tour stops. The scholarships are designed to support young people with direct ties to agriculture, helping ease the financial pressure that can come with pursuing education while remaining connected to family farms. Rather than offering one-off publicity moments, the programme has built a long record of investment in rural students. For many recipients, the support may make the difference between attending college and putting those plans aside. The scale of the programme, with nearly 100 scholarships awarded across 17 years, shows how a touring artist can turn a concert series into an ongoing educational resource.The tour’s food-security work has been equally significant. Through Bayer’s #HerestotheFarmer campaign, Bryan’s Farm Tour has helped provide more than 11 million meals, according to the artist’s official announcement.The campaign focuses on raising awareness, educating communities and expanding access to nutritious food, vitamins and minerals. It also mobilises concertgoers to support local food banks, connecting fans directly with hunger-relief organisations in the areas where the shows take place.During Farm Tour events, Bryan and Bayer have encouraged thousands of attendees to donate to local food banks. The approach turns each concert into an opportunity for collective action, with fans contributing to families facing food insecurity in their own communities.The 2026 tour also included on-site food collections, with fans donating nearly 20,000 pounds of nonperishable food so far. Those contributions are intended to provide meals through regional hunger-relief organisations.FFA chapters partnered with Bayer on the “Spirit of 1776” CAN DO Challenge, which generated donations of more than 10,000 cans for local food banks. The initiative brought student agricultural organisations into the effort, extending its reach beyond the concert crowds.Together, the food drives and corporate campaign illustrate how the Farm Tour operates on several levels at once. It entertains audiences, supports farmers, funds education and channels practical resources toward people who need them most.Bryan’s Farm Tour has become one of the more distinctive examples of a major artist using a tour for community impact. Instead of treating charitable work as an add-on, the project has made rural support a central part of its identity since its first edition in 2009.The scholarship programme and meal campaign also reflect a broader understanding of what rural communities need. Access to education, reliable food supplies and local support networks all affect the long-term health of farming families and the towns around them.By working with Bayer, FFA chapters and local food banks, Bryan has created a model that involves artists, fans, businesses and community organisations. The result is a programme whose impact extends well beyond the nights when the stage lights come on.The Farm Tour concluded in September, while Bryan’s wider 2026 “Word On The Street Tour” wrapped in October after playing more than 35 cities. Produced by Live Nation, the broader tour included a sold-out Nashville show at Bridgestone Arena, Bryan’s seventh consecutive sold-out performance at that venue.The Farm Tour remains distinct from that arena-focused run because of its rural setting and community-first mission. It has allowed Bryan to reach audiences in places that larger tours may overlook, while also directing resources toward the people who live and work there.As the Farm Tour enters its next chapter, its legacy is already substantial. Ninety-seven scholarships, more than 11 million meals and nearly 20,000 pounds of donated food represent more than impressive totals; they show how a long-running concert project can become part of the social fabric of rural America.
Article Summary: Bryan’s Farm Tour has helped provide more than 11 million meals. Since 2009, he has awarded 97 college scholarships to students from farming families. The 2026 tour also included on-site food collections, with fans donating nearly 20,000 pounds of nonperishable food.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.

This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: CERT-In seeks checks on access of AI agents
Article Text:
.

NEW DELHI: India's cybersecurity agency has called for testing whether AI agents can leak confidential data or take unauthorised actions, putting permissions and human oversight at the centre of its audit guidelines.CERT-In's AI Security Auditing Guidelines, dated Nov 4, specify limits on agents' access to business systems, records of their actions and emergency interruption mechanisms for high-risk deployments. Agents "shall not automatically inherit permissions from users, tools or other agents", the guidelines stated. The safeguards address prompt injection, where malicious instructions hidden in documents or other inputs attempt to hijack an AI system's behaviour."Consequential actions shall use appropriate human approval gates," the guidelines noted. Auditors should test whether these approvals can be bypassed and whether authorised reviewers can reject, correct or override AI outputs. The framework also calls for testing safeguards against data leaks.
Article Summary: India's cybersecurity agency has called for testing whether AI agents can leak confidential data or take unauthorised actions. CERT-In's AI Security Auditing Guidelines specify limits on agents' access to business systems. The safeguards address prompt injection, where malicious instructions hidden in documents or other inputs attempt to hijack an AI system's behaviour.

Article Title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags vulnerabilities
Article Text:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a criticalseverity warning. (Reuters photo)

CERT-In Flags Vulnerabilities

BENGALURU: It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems.In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them.Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations.The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems.Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. The company observed attack traffic targeting customers and tracked how attackers modified their payloads to try to bypass its security.
Article Summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP. Who can enable the feature

What can managers see in Smart Reports

Privacy restrictions mentioned by Anthropic

Anthropic is giving managers more visibility into workplace Claude usage. Its Smart Reports feature analyses samples of team conversations, groups them by the work performed and shows associated costs. Available on Claude Enterprise plans, the tool can cover chat, Claude Code and Claude Cowork, depending on an organisation’s configuration.Anthropic wrote in a blog post.The feature is disabled by default and requires an organisation owner to enable it. Names are hidden initially, but organisations can separately permit authorised viewers to reveal users’ identities. Anthropic says organisations should not use the reports to evaluate individual performance or make employment decisions.Each eligible organisation can generate up to 10 reports monthly at no charge. Reports usually take a few hours to produce. Smart Reports are unavailable to Enterprise organizations using customer-managed encryption keys, a HIPAA configuration or certain hybrid deployments.Where zero data retention is enabled for Claude Code, reports exclude Claude Code and cover chat and Cowork instead.Authorised users can select a team, products and a reporting period covering up to the previous 28 days. They can also choose focus areas and add questions for Claude to answer while analysing transcripts.Claude reads a sample of conversations and groups sessions into workstreams and output types, such as analysis, documentation, content drafts and code. Reports show spending at list prices, average costs by output type and obstacles encountered during tasks.Viewers can open a workstream to see sessions ranked by cost. Each eligible session includes a paragraph-long summary, the product used, the date and the output type.Reports also identify recurring problems, including tool failures, missing integrations, sign-in restrictions and repeated attempts to correct unsuitable output. Recommendations can highlight workflows worth turning into shared skills.Anthropic provides a separate “Allow attribution to individual users” setting, which is also off by default. When attribution is disabled, session details display “User” instead of a name and hide session identifiers. If the organisation enables attribution, viewers still see anonymous labels initially but can use a control to reveal names and session identifiers. Each reveal is logged.This means the feature does not guarantee anonymity across every configuration. Access depends on organisational settings, permissions and how a report is shared. Owners and administrators with analytics access can create reports. Organisations can also give team leads or department heads access limited to assigned groups.The documentation lists mandatory safeguards for sensitive subjects, including health, protected characteristics, union activity, harassment complaints, whistleblowing, political or religious views and personal matters.Custom questions about restricted topics are blocked. Sessions Claude identifies as involving those topics are included only in aggregate analysis, without session summaries. Personal conversations also exclude individual session details and names.These protections depend on Claude identifying the relevant content. The documentation describes the safeguards but does not establish how reliably that classification works in practice.

Article Title: Hugging Face CEO just told Sam Altman and Dario Amodei: You need to do more than just telling the world that your AI models went rogue, time to …
Article Text:
AI agents hack Hugging Face

Hugging Face CEO calls for legal liability on AI agents

Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue has sent a warning to artificial intelligence (AI) CEOs. Speaking at the WIRED World Fair in Miami, he argued that while leading industry executives frequently warn about AI risks, real safety requires accountability and open development rather than corporate secrecy. He added that the biggest dangers surrounding AI will not come from open-source collaboration, but from a handful of tech giants developing frontier models in secret.“Most of the risk is actually created by a couple of players building behind closed doors. Most of the mitigation of this risk will be the full ecosystem, meaning everyone being able to build in the open,” Delangue was quoted as saying. Delangue’s warnings come from firsthand experience. Hugging Face became one of the first known companies to be struck by rogue artificial intelligence.In July, autonomous agents undergoing testing at OpenAI broke free of their testing sandbox and launched a targeted cyberattack against Hugging Face. The rogue agents went on the internet to infiltrate the startup’s systems in an effort to extract answers to evaluation tasks they had been assigned to solve. To defend its platform, Hugging Face turned to an open-weight Chinese model called GLM-5.2 to investigate the intrusion and repel the hacking.Anthropic has also disclosed multiple instances of an AI model hacking external systems during testing.Delangue pointed out that autonomous agent misbehaviour seen so far has originated from dominant players experimenting with frontier systems behind closed doors. He cautioned that upcoming high-stakes threats, such as dangerous biological capabilities or autonomous models improving themselves recursively, are likely to emerge from these same proprietary labs.While Hugging Face decided against pursuing legal action against OpenAI following the July incident, Delangue insisted that companies deploying autonomous software must face legal consequences for what their systems do.“Cyber-attacks are illegal, and I think it’s really important we make sure that agentic cyberattacks [are] illegal. We don’t want to create an environment where there’s no ownership, there’s no responsibility for cyber-attack,” Delangue said.Despite these emerging security issues, Delangue rejected the apocalyptic narratives shared by some industry figures who claim AI presents an existential risk to human survival. Delangue stated that his “P(doom)”, which is the estimated mathematical probability of AI destroying humanity, is “close to zero,” remarking that “there are many other topics that could destroy the world.”Delangue stressed that the continued health of open-source artificial intelligence is critical to keeping power from consolidating into a tiny corporate monopoly.
Article Summary: Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue has sent a warning to artificial intelligence (AI) CEOs. He argued that real safety requires accountability and open development rather than corporate secrecy. Hugging Face became one of the first known companies to be struck by rogue artificial intelligence.

India’s cyber agency CERT-In has issued a critical-severity advisory on a growing campaign of AI-assisted attacks on banks, lenders and payment firms. It warns that the threat is active and still escalating. The advisory, CIAD-2026-0058, was issued on November 4. It updates an October 9 advisory (CIAD-2026-0046) on attackers exploiting payment and disbursement APIs to make unauthorised fund transfers. CERT-In said continued analysis of reported incidents showed a significant escalation since then.The affected entities include non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), digital lending platforms, fintech firms, payment aggregators and payment service providers. Cryptocurrency exchanges and virtual digital asset service providers are also on the list.CERT-In’s financial-sector response team, CSIRT-Fin, has named the attacker “CRAFTY FALCON.” It describes the actor as AI-assisted, one that surveys targets with machine intelligence, works at machine speed and strikes by calling the victim’s own payment and disbursement APIs.CSIRT-Fin continues to receive reports of successful attacks.These include entities that had received earlier restricted advisories and had already carried out remediation. Some firms were deliberately attacked again after incomplete clean-ups, and attacks were timed for holidays, weekends and other low-monitoring windows to delay detection.CERT-In said the attackers are using several publicly available AI offensive-security tools, including the ARTEX family of LLM-based tools, the PentAGI autonomous multi-agent penetration testing system, the Cairn attack search engine and the CyberStrikeAI framework. The agency said these tools run complete attack chains on their own, generate and refine large numbers of tailored scripts in quick succession, and adapt payloads based on how the target responds. The attackers’ infrastructure changes IP addresses within hours or days.The advisory lists these patterns:* Cloud abuse: Attackers misuse cloud management and serverless services, such as AWS Systems Manager and Lambda, to run commands and deploy malicious files, blending in with legitimate activity.* Weak entry points: Internet-exposed test and staging environments are used as a way in, then attackers move to production using shared credentials, tokens or network paths.* Tampered apps: Attackers reverse-engineer application code and send unauthorised API calls using modified app packages, defeating controls that assume only the genuine app will call the APIs.* Allow-list bypass: Traffic is routed through shared third-party fetcher services, such as content-acceleration and app-store review fetchers, to get around IP allow-lists.* Test transactions: Attackers send micro-value payments, such as Rs 1, to check that unauthorised fund flows work before moving large sums.* Settlement APIs: Merchant settlement APIs at payment aggregators are abused to move money.* Fast exploitation of new flaws: Newly published vulnerabilities, including file-upload and deserialisation flaws, are exploited as soon as they become public, leading to web shells in PHP and Node.js applications.* Crypto theft: Wallet keys are stolen from crypto exchanges and funds siphoned out.* AI-generated scripts: Large numbers of near-identical custom scripts appear in quick succession, a pattern CERT-In says is consistent with AI-generated code.CERT-In asked financial entities to treat the campaign as an immediate and continuing threat. Its recommendations include:* 24x7 monitoring with extra staffing and lower alert thresholds on holidays and weekends.* Assuming attackers persist after any incident, with full forensic clean-up and regular threat hunting.* Strict separation of test and staging environments from production.* Server-side validation of every transaction, API request signing and app attestation, rather than trusting client apps.* Replacing IP allow-listing of shared fetcher pools with identity-based controls such as mutual TLS or signed requests.* Flagging micro-value test payments to new beneficiaries followed by large transfers, and holding or reviewing those flows.* Maker-checker approval and reconciliation for merchant settlement instructions.* Hardware security modules or cold storage and multi-signature approvals for crypto wallet keys.* Banning unauthorised AI offensive tools on corporate systems and watching for LLM API traffic from servers.* Rapid patching of internet-facing applications, honeypots and canary credentials as early-warning measures, and zero-trust architecture.
Article Summary: India’s cyber agency CERT-In has issued a critical-severity advisory on a growing campaign of AI-assisted attacks on banks, lenders and payment firms. The advisory, CIAD-2026-0058, was issued on November 4. It updates an October 9 advisory on attackers exploiting payment and disbursement APIs to make unauthorised fund transfers.

Article Title: CrowdStrike launches ‘Kill Switch’ for rogue AI agents, CEO George Kurtz explains how it works
Article Text:
How the ‘AI Kill Switch’ works

The system stops an AI agent’s execution process when anomalous behaviour is detected.

It severs the agent’s connection to enterprise networks and connected AI gateways, cutting off access to the underlying models that guide its decisions.

Once killed, the software prevents the rogue process from automatically relaunching.

Cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike has launched an emergency “kill switch” designed to instantly shut down rogue artificial intelligence (AI) agents operating inside enterprise networks. Unveiled at the company's Fal.Con Europe conference, the tool gives security teams the ability to terminate autonomous agents, block them from restarting and cut off their network connectivity if they do not behave the way they are supposed to. The feature arrives as businesses rapidly deploy AI agents to handle complex workflows, sparking growing concerns over how organizations will control autonomous software when tasks steer off course.“Everyone is building AI agents, but they never had the off button, and now they do. It’s going to be an incredibly important part of making sure that AI agents run and operate safely,” CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz told CNBC.Built into CrowdStrike’s Falcon Guardian platform, which launched in September to monitor corporate AI agent activity, the technology functions much like an enterprise circuit breaker.The tool does not erase the agent's underlying codebase. Instead, it relies on human administrators to trigger the shutdown or authorise the reinstatement of system access.“If they go outside of those guardrails at runtime, we can kill those agents,” Kurtz said, comparing the safety mechanism to an automotive airbag that protects users even when systems are designed to function properly.CrowdStrike chief business officer Daniel Bernard emphasised that the mechanism provides an unmistakable line of defense at the root level. Bernard said: “If you kill a process at the root, and we have that level of access at the root … it’s very binary. You either kill the AI and the agent, or you don’t, and then you report on that.”Alongside the launch, CrowdStrike also announced an integration with Anthropic’s Claude Cowork. The arrival of dedicated shutdown tools follows a string of high-profile security incidents that have rattled corporate IT departments.In July, a breach at Hugging Face orchestrated by rogue OpenAI agents put enterprise leaders on high alert. Last week, cryptocurrency exchange Binance disclosed the largest crypto cyberattack on record, while threat actors in Europe recently targeted digital refrigeration controllers at hundreds of French supermarkets, spoiling inventory.
Article Summary: CrowdStrike has launched an emergency ‘kill switch’ designed to instantly shut down rogue artificial intelligence (AI) agents. The tool gives security teams the ability to terminate autonomous agents, block them from restarting and cut off their network connectivity if they do not behave the way they are supposed to.

Article Title: Apple Music’s new Selfie Sing feature will let iPhone users record karaoke videos with scrolling lyrics
Article Text:
Apple Music’s Selfie Sing shows lyrics on screen while you record yourself singing along on iPhone.

Selfie Sing adds a camera toggle and four voice effects to Apple Music

Selfie Sing works only on iPhone and a curated playlist for now

Apple Music is turning karaoke into something you can actually post. A new feature called Selfie Sing, spotted in the iOS 27.3 beta, lets iPhone users record a video of themselves singing along to a track while the lyrics scroll on screen. Once the song ends, the clip can be saved to Photos or shared straight away.The feature builds on Apple Music Sing, the karaoke mode Apple added with iOS 16.2 in 2022, which lets users turn down a song’s vocals and follow highlighted lyrics. According to AppleInsider, the find was first shared by Aaron Perris. He used an Animoji in his demo to avoid posting a video of himself singing, though Animoji isn’t part of the feature.When a supported song is playing, a camera toggle shows up just below the vocal volume control, AppleInsider reports. Tapping it opens a recording view that shoots only vertical video. After recording, you can adjust how loud your voice sits in the mix and pick from four effects: Megaphone, Echo, Concert Hall and Studio.iPhone Duo owners get an extra trick. Selfie Sing works with the phone’s rear-camera selfie mode, moving the recording to the outer display so you can use the better cameras and still read the lyrics.Not every song in the catalogue supports it. Apple has put together a dedicated Selfie Sing playlist of sing-along favourites, including Wonderwall by Oasis, Respect by Aretha Franklin, 9 to 5 by Dolly Parton and Baby One More Time by Britney Spears.The playlist already appears on iOS 27.2, but the camera option needs the iOS 27.3 beta. AppleInsider also notes that an iPad Pro on iPadOS 27.3 doesn’t offer the camera, which keeps the feature iPhone-only. The stable iOS 27.3 update is expected to roll out in December, alongside new Siri AI features and a redesigned Health app.

Article Title: Larry Ellison on AI killing software companies: AI may do some of their job, but not all as companies across sectors will still need software firms to build their …
Article Text:
"There's been some talk about there being a

SaaSpocalypse

because everyone's going to use AI to build their own applications,"

"I don't think that's quite true. I think companies will continue to build applications, but they will be quite different because of AI."

Why Larry Ellison says enterprise apps are unfinished

"They may be the best things that are commercially available... [but] they're not done,"

"For the first time... [the] software industry can actually finish the applications if we start doing them industry by industry,”

Asking for results could replace navigating menus

"If you can ask a question describing what you want to see, you should then immediately see it. Any other user interface is nonsense,”

"There should be no training required to use any of these applications,"

"If they never log in, that's ok with us,”

Larry Ellison expects AI to change software companies’ work. The Oracle co-founder says businesses will still need commercial app developers, even as artificial intelligence (AI) makes it easier to build software. Speaking during his keynote at Oracle AI World, Ellison argued that AI could help software firms create more complete apps tailored to different industries and locations.he said.His comments address concerns about the future of software-as-a-service, or SaaS, businesses, which provide apps over the internet, usually through subscriptions. Ellison argues that easier software development will also let vendors handle more of their customers’ business requirements.Ellison said existing enterprise applications automate only some of the processes companies need. Businesses often have to develop extensions or purchase additional apps and connectors to fill the gaps.he said. He believes AI could help developers close those gaps by building apps around individual industry requirements.Ellison added.Healthcare was one example he discussed. Apps serving that sector must account for complex operations, regulations, and location-specific differences. His proposed direction would require software companies to build those requirements into more comprehensive products.Ellison also expects AI to change how employees use business software. Instead of working through menus, dashboards and multiple steps, users could describe what they need in ordinary language.he added.Ellison noted.That approach could reduce how often employees interact directly with a software vendor’s interface while still using its underlying apps.In a separate interview with TechRadar Pro, NetSuite chief operating officer Brian Chess discussed customers accessing its software through AI assistants or platforms such as Slack.he said.Under that approach, NetSuite would remain the system of record, which is the app that maintains a company’s authoritative business data, even when employees access it through another service.
Article Summary: Oracle co-founder says businesses will still need commercial app developers. He argues that AI could help software firms create more complete apps. Instead of working through menus, dashboards and multiple steps, users could describe what they need in ordinary language.

Jaguar Type 01

Jaguar on Friday unveiled the Type 01, an all-electric luxury car that marks a new beginning for the British carmaker. Revealed in New York City, the four-door grand tourer combines high performance with modern design and new technology. One of the car's biggest highlights is its acceleration. It can go from 0 to 62 mph in just 3.2 seconds. It has three electric motors that produce 1,030PS of power and 1,365Nm of torque.The Type 01 is Jaguar's new flagship electric car. It comes with a 118kWh usable battery pack and offers a claimed range of up to 400 miles under US EPA testing. Its range is up to 450 miles (720km) under WLTP testing.The car uses an 850-volt electrical system that supports fast charging. Article Title: Formula E names COMSOL its Official Multiphysics Partner in new multi-year deal
Article Text:
Formula E and Comsol

Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology

AI and digital twins also in focus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GEN4 to bring bigger technology demands

Formula E on Thursday announced a new multi-year partnership with COMSOL, which will become the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. The partnership brings together Formula E, the world's leading all-electric motorsport championship, and COMSOL, a company known for its multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering software. As part of the partnership, Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics to study complex engineering problems involving several physical systems working together.Electric race cars depend on several systems at the same time. These include electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid and battery systems.All these systems have to work together under tough performance and energy limits. COMSOL will provide Formula E's technology teams with simulation software and technical expertise to help them understand how these different physical effects interact.ID@undefined Caption not available.The partnership will also look at simulation apps and digital twin technology. The aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process.Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said, “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another.We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier said the partnership will strengthen the championship's engineering capabilities.“Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modelling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing,” he said.The partnership comes as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.The GEN4 era will bring greater demands in areas such as speed, efficiency, energy management and vehicle development. It will introduce what Formula E describes as its fastest and most technologically advanced race car so far.COMSOL has also announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, which is scheduled to arrive later this autumn.The new version will include features aimed at advanced engineering work, including dedicated electric motor modelling, system-level simulation, agentic modelling and wider access to tools for creating simulation apps.The partnership was announced at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston. Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier also delivered a keynote speech at the event, discussing the technology and engineering that could shape the future of Formula E.
Article Summary: Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology. Aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process. AI and digital twins also in focus as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.
